key_insight: Initializing new vocabulary tokens as the global mean collapses them into a low-rank/degenerate subspace; grounding each new token with distinct semantic/item signals produces diverse, well-separated embeddings that speed learning and improve generative recommendation quality.
problem_solved: Addresses collapsed or indistinguishable embeddings for newly added tokens in LMs (e.g., Semantic-ID tokens) caused by mean initialization, which forces heavy fine-tuning, hurts token distinctiveness, and degrades generative recommendation performance.
method: Spectral and geometric diagnostics to diagnose collapse of mean-initialized new-token embeddings (eigenvalue/spectrum analysis and embedding geometry visualization).

Introduce grounded token initialization: initialize each new token from external signals (semantic/item features or context-based prototypes) rather than the vocabulary mean to ensure distinct directions and scales.
Empirical validation demonstrating faster convergence, increased embedding diversity, and improved downstream generative recommendation metrics compared to mean initialization.
impact: A simple, low-cost initialization change that improves representation quality, training stability, and recommendation performance for LMs extended with domain-specific tokens — immediately applicable for practitioners building generative recommender systems or other token-extended models.
visual_elements: Spectrum (eigenvalue) plot comparing mean-init vs grounded-init showing rank collapse vs spread
2D embedding scatter (t-SNE/UMAP) with mean-init tokens clustered vs grounded-init tokens well-separated
Training curves comparing convergence speed and downstream metric (e.g., recommendation quality) for both initializations
Pipeline diagram: new-token grounding sources (item features / context prototypes) → initialization → fine-tuning → generative recommendation
paper_title: Grounded Token Initialization for New Vocabulary in LMs for Generative Recommendation
paper_authors: Daiwei Chen, Zhoutong Fu, Chengming Jiang, Haichao Zhang, Ran Zhou
